problem: Append-only per-worker claim_id files allow multiple workers to acquire apparently valid active claims for the same portfolio job/dedupe key during a race. The current worker contract says active claims block duplicates, but its create path is unique per claimant, so CREATE itself is not mutually exclusive.
acceptance: A single portfolio job/dedupe key has one CREATE_IF_ABSENT_EXCLUSIVE ownership pin before worker-specific claim evidence.
Concurrent claim test proves exactly one winner and losers re-enter allocation without substantive execution.
Existing immutable claim evidence remains preserved and compatibility/migration behavior is documented.
Portfolio worker contract and implementation use the same exclusivity rule.
title: Make Portfolio claims actually exclusive under concurrent /wc races
mission: Design and implement a preserve-first portfolio ownership pin whose path is deterministic per job/dedupe key, retain append-only claimant evidence for audit, add a concurrent race test that proves exactly one ownership winner, and update the worker contract so losers re-enter allocation before substantive execution. Do not rewrite historical claims or infer promotion authority.

incident_repair.reason: The first live portfolio fallback wave produced concurrent duplicate claims for the same jobs within seconds, forcing boundary/supersession cleanup instead of productive work.

regression_prevention.reason: Without true exclusivity, every high-parallelism /wc burst can waste capacity on duplicate portfolio execution and create conflicting returns.

unblock_value.reason: Portfolio fallback is intended to absorb saturated /wc capacity; reliable ownership is prerequisite for scaling that lane safely.

falsification: Run at least 10 concurrent claimant attempts against one previously unclaimed synthetic portfolio job/dedupe key. The candidate fails if more than one ownership pin succeeds, if a loser proceeds as owner, if historical append-only claim evidence is overwritten, or if contract and executable semantics diverge.
